perspective:
From Maria’s direct perspective, I know:

- I work with Cheryl at the community center; we are colleagues and have collaborated before, and we’ve talked about our different cultural backgrounds and personal experiences.
- I saw Cheryl looking stressed and overwhelmed with paperwork and planning for a new outreach project.
- I offered to help her, and she accepted, saying she could definitely use the help.
- After helping, I observed Cheryl handling her responsibilities better and showing more confidence.
- At a staff meeting, I suggested Cheryl for a leadership role, saying she had shown great aptitude and commitment.
- The team leader agreed with my suggestion and asked Cheryl what she thought.
- Cheryl thanked me and said she was ready to take on the challenge.
- Later, I privately worried that my suggestion might have seemed like overstepping, so I told Cheryl I wanted her to feel supported, not pressured.
- Cheryl told me she had been a bit surprised, but she appreciated my support and said it meant a lot that I believed in her.
- I felt relieved that she valued my honesty and support.
- I then proposed that we co-lead the project together.
- Cheryl said that sounded fantastic, called my guidance invaluable, and said we make a great team.
- After several successful collaborations, I told Cheryl our work together had been fruitful and asked if she wanted to team up on future projects.
- Cheryl said she would love that, that working with me had been a wonderful experience, and that she was excited about what we could achieve together.
